questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I've been in Amsterdam quite a lot because of familyy loving there, and have always felt a big connection to the city. So going there on exchange was the perfect opportunity for me to try and live there.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The exchange coordinators at science park were excellent at giving us all the information we needed. they always responded to my emails super fast.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a science introduction day at campus that really helped in getting an overview of everything. I also met some great people that day

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was in a lottery through the university. We were told that there was a 50% chance of getting something, which was a bit nerve-racking, especially because we didn't know if we got anything until 2 months before... But it seemed like almost everyone at Science got housing this year which was great:)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You have no influence on what area of the city you're gonna get, it's completely random. But if you do get something to live in, my advice would be to just take it. I lived 10 km away from the campus, but it was still worth it as its way cheaper and easier than having to find something on your own.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I ended up doing a minor which i found perfect in terms of registration because there were no overlaps in the schedule that you had to think about, and a certain amount of spots were already reserved for exchange students.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There's a course catalogue, its a bit confusing to find but when you figure it out its a great way to get an overview of the possibilities

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the minor that I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you see a minor that you find interesting it's definitely the easiest thing to do as an exchange student. Also you're in the same class for the whole semester which also makes it easier to connect with your classmates.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was a bit lower than I expected, probably because I have a molecular background i'd hoped there was more biology in general. But there were so many different students doing the minor, which ment that it could get a bit superficial for me at times.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: We mostly had lectures even though it said in the schedule that we would also have a lot of seminars, but that didn't really happen. I missed having to solve more problems, as that is how I normally learn the best. But because we were only around 35 people in the class the lectures were also very down to earth which i liked. Pretty sure that it depends on the course though, ive met a lot of people who had a completely different experience.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Minor in Neurobiology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would say that it makes the most sense to do all three courses from the minor if you're interested in neuroscience, as they are all very integrated. For me personally the level of the courses was a bit different from what I expected, but on the other hand i feel like Ive gotten a pretty good overview of the brain og neuroscience. And because of the level, I also had a lot of freetime which has been amazing, also because I didn't go for academic reasons...

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didnt really join anything but they have a lot of things you can do:)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All sorts

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: CREA is a great place to do all sorts of creative stuff from dancing to painting

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are sooo many things to do in Amsterdam, just get a bike and explore

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy, I felt at home already a few hours after arrival

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Do a minor

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language is silly and I never learned it

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The art scene, concerts, theaters, clubs, bars, community kitchens, squads, jazz. Its amazing

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Do some easy courses so you have time to have fun. Go to the introduction week, it's a great way to meet people. Be open to everything.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just have patience in the beginning. It takes time to adapt and to meet the right people. But you'll get there and then its gonna most amazing months

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Amsterdam is very multicultural, and Ive met so many different people from all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: You really have to get out of your conform zone and talk to people if you wanna make friends.. But its great and you learn so much from it!

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Just go!!!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
